meta.title: ODLAR: one consistent fire record and risk map
meta.description: A platform that harmonizes NASA's MODIS and VIIRS satellite archives, builds burning-activity calendars and shows today's fire risk against 25 years of history. Pilot: Azerbaijan and the South Caucasus.

home.eyebrow: NASA Space Apps 2026 · MODIS & VIIRS Hot Spots
home.title: 25 years of fire. <hl>One consistent record.</hl>
home.lead: ODLAR stitches NASA's two satellite fire archives together, builds a burning-activity calendar for every region, and shows today's risk against 25 years of history.
home.regionsAtRisk: {count, plural, =0 {no regions at high risk} one {# region at high risk} other {# regions at high risk}}

split.title: The record is <hl>split in two</hl>
split.s1: MODIS on Terra and Aqua sees the ground in 1 km pixels. Most small field and stubble fires slip through.
split.s2: VIIRS at 375 m catches far smaller fires. Overnight, the number of recorded fires multiplies.
split.s3t: That jump is the sensor, not the fire
split.s3: Trends computed on the raw record show growth that never happened, and AI trained on it learns the wrong lesson.
split.s4: Using the years both sensors flew together, we calibrate MODIS to the VIIRS scale per region and season, and carry the uncertainty all the way through.
split.chartAria: Annual fire detections in the South Caucasus: raw vs harmonized

clock.title: Every region has its own <hl>fire clock</hl>
clock.lead: Each ring is a year, each slice a week. Season onset, peak weeks, the end of the season and unusual years are all found automatically.

audiences.title: Depth for scientists, <hl>clarity for citizens</hl>
audiences.sci: Interactive map, raw vs harmonized comparison, trend analysis, a calendar for any area you draw, and data export through an open API.
audiences.cit: Pick your district, see the risk in plain words and get an alert when it rises. Signing up takes a minute.

riskNow.title: Where the risk is <hl>high right now</hl>
riskNow.lead: The short-term model combines the harmonized history with temperature, humidity, wind, rainfall and vegetation.

pipeline.title: From satellite <hl>to alert</hl>
pipeline.s1: NASA FIRMS (MODIS C6.1, VIIRS S-NPP / NOAA-20 / NOAA-21), NASA POWER weather, NDVI, Open-Meteo forecasts.
pipeline.s2: Quantile mapping per region and season, conditional bias correction, and block-bootstrap uncertainty.
pipeline.s3: Season onset, peak weeks, critical windows and unusual years, all on one consistent record.
pipeline.s4: LightGBM: a calibrated probability for the next 7 days, a 13-week season outlook, and the reasons behind each.

why.title: The window to stitch the archive <hl>is closing</hl>
why.lead: The overlap period, when both sensors fly at once, is the only basis for calibration. Once it ends, building one consistent archive gets much harder.

footer.tagline: One fire history for the Land of Fire.
footer.credits: NASA FIRMS, NASA POWER, Open-Meteo, OpenStreetMap, geoBoundaries, OpenFreeMap
footer.challenge: Built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.
footer.disclaimer: ODLAR is not an official warning service. In an emergency call 112.

compare.title: Harmonization lab
compare.lead: Put the raw and harmonized records side by side, and inspect the calibration function and how it was validated.
compare.transferLead: A MODIS weekly count against the VIIRS value at the same quantile, by season. The steeper the curve, the more fires MODIS misses.
compare.validationLead: Each year from 2012 on is held out of the calibration, its MODIS data harmonized, and the result compared with what VIIRS actually saw that year.

methodology.title: Methodology
methodology.lead: Every step of ODLAR: data sources, quality control, harmonization, validation, the calendar and the risk model. The limitations are stated openly too.

data.title: Data & API
data.lead: Download harmonized series, annual totals and fire detections, or integrate directly through the API.
data.apiLead: Every endpoint returns JSON. No key is needed; requests are rate-limited per IP.
data.licenseText: Source data: NASA FIRMS (public domain), NASA POWER, OpenStreetMap (ODbL), geoBoundaries. The harmonized product is shared under CC BY 4.0.

report.title: Fire report
report.calendar: Burning calendar, week by week (harmonized detections)
report.about1: Counts are NASA FIRMS active-fire detections (MODIS since 2000, VIIRS since 2012) put on one scale (harmonized), so years before and after 2012 can be compared.
report.about2: A detection is a heat signal seen from space, not burned area or a count of separate fires. Clouds and smoke hide some fires; hatched weeks had no satellite observation.
report.about3: Weather: Open-Meteo forecast and NASA POWER history. Forecast reliability is from tests on past years the models never saw.
